record.original_question: Let H : Top0 -> Set be an irreducible subset system, and let SH-Sob denote the category of super H-sober spaces with continuous mappings. Is SH-Sob reflective in Top0? Equivalently, for every T0 space X, does there exist a super H-sobrification of X?

evidence.quote: Question 1.8. For an R-subset system H : Top0 -> Set, is SH-Sob reflective in Top0? Or equivalently, for any T0 space X, does the super H-sobrification of X exist?
A full subcategory D of a category C is called reflective if the inclusion functor has a left adjoint, which then is called a reflector([1]).
Additionally, we give positive answers to Question 1.3~Question 1.8.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbf{Top}_0$ denote the category of $T_0$ topological spaces with continuous maps, and let $\mathbf{Set}$ denote the category of sets. An irreducible subset system (R-subset system) is a functor $H:\mathbf{Top}_0\to\mathbf{Set}$ assigning to each $T_0$ space $X$ a collection $H(X)$ of irreducible subsets of $X$, in a way that is preserved (in the appropriate sense) under continuous maps. A $T_0$ space $X$ is called super $H$-sober if for every continuous map $f:Y\to X$ from a $T_0$ space $Y$ and every $A\in H(Y)$, the image closure $\overline{f(A)}$ has a (unique) generic point in $X$ — equivalently, $X$ satisfies the appropriate sobriety-type condition with respect to all irreducible sets selected by $H$ on arbitrary $T_0$ spaces. Let $S_H\text{-}\mathbf{Sob}$ denote the full subcategory of $\mathbf{Top}_0$ consisting of super $H$-sober spaces.

Recall that a full subcategory $\mathcal{D}$ of a category $\mathcal{C}$ is reflective if the inclusion functor $\mathcal{D}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{C}$ has a left adjoint.

Question: For an arbitrary irreducible subset system $H:\mathbf{Top}_0\to\mathbf{Set}$, is $S_H\text{-}\mathbf{Sob}$ a reflective subcategory of $\mathbf{Top}_0$? Equivalently, does every $T_0$ space $X$ admit a super $H$-sobrification?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is reported as resolved positively: for every irreducible (R-) subset system $H$, the category of super $H$-sober spaces is reflective in $\mathbf{Top}_0$, so every $T_0$ space has a super $H$-sobrification.

status_evidence.title: Super H-sober spaces and H-sobrifications (arXiv:2109.11299)
status_evidence.snippet: Positive answers are given to questions concerning reflectivity of super H-sober spaces in Top0 and existence of super H-sobrifications.
status_evidence.claim: The reflectivity question for super H-sober spaces is answered affirmatively.
